utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic, did you have --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have your dental appointment this morning? THE ACCUSED NALETILIC: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I had my tooth pulled out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How are you feeling now? THE ACCUSED NALETILIC: [Interpretation] Well, not particularly nice, but I'll manage. It will be all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Prosecutor, please continue with your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. But first I would like to tell that yesterday somehow escaped a very important piece of our traditional presentation of the case. The testimony of this witness will go mostly to paragraph 7, 8, 11 of the background; paragraphs 14 to 16, superior authority; general allegations, paragraph 18 to 21; count 1, paragraphs 25, 27, 34(a), (b); counts from 2 to 5, paragraph 36; counts 9 to 12, paragraphs 45, 46. Thank you very much, and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Salko Osmic, are you all right today?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, sir, yes, I'm feeling better today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's return to yesterday's testimony. Do you remember the date when you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 20th of April, '92 -- no, '93. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Perhaps you remember the approximate time when it happened. I don't mean the exact hour, but morning, noon, evening?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened around 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask you that we go into private session for some minutes, because now I intend to ask the witness some questions, and he may give some names that should be protected at this stage at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Osmic, do you remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Wait, wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Open session].

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Osmic, do you remember the name of the location you were taken to after the arrest?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were captured on a hill called Pomen. But as far as I can remember, the place that we were taken to was out of the village of Orlovac or the village of Stupari. I cannot say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was it far away from Sovici?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. It's the lower part of Sovici, so called Doljani. It's nearer Jablanica about 10 kilometres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yesterday, you claimed that there was a sort of command where you were taken to after the arrest. Could you describe in general terms the location you were taken to, the premises, building, or something else?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was, as far as I could see -- although I didn't have much opportunity to see because beating ensued straight away. But as far as I can remember, there was a playground of sorts that we had to cross, under beating, and there was a wooden shack where the prisoners were interrogated. And those who were more familiar with the area were saying that there was a fish pond, a fish farm, there, but I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You just told the Court that they started beating you immediately when you were taken to that area, to the pond as they call it. Who were the people who started beating arrested people?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the three of us who were arrested last, we fell into the hands of a bloodthirsty executioner, and I will call him that. He was called Cikota. He took us over, and he beat us until we reached the wooden shack, and in it was that commander of theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see what was happening to other prisoners who were taken to the same place while you were beaten, being beaten?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the other six, they had been beaten before. Only after a while, I saw the upshot of it all. And as for the three of us, we could not lift our heads from the ground because one of the -- because one of the soldiers had his foot on my head all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You just told the Court that the man who was beating you and two others was called Cikota. Could you describe that person.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is a sturdy, well-built man. I presume an athlete, about two metres tall. I mean really big. Brown hair, cut short. Well, that will be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was he dressed in uniform or in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see his insignia, badges?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really remember, but we heard that he was a rather good soldier, that he had been awarded all possible Croatian decorations. But as for the patches, I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see that man before?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And where did you learn his name?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in Ljubuski, a day or two later perhaps, we found a Croatian newspaper. I can't remember which one. So we leafed through it, and we came across an article, and I recognised Cikota, the man who beat us. And after that, men who had taken us to Ljubuski in that van came, and they were looking for us because we were the last ones to arrive. And they told us that we had been in luck, and that had we stayed an hour or two longer, we would have all been killed because Cikota had allegedly been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Were you interrogated in the fish pond, let's say, area?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some questions on the basis of which they could beat you. There were no questions that were really important, because we didn't know any answers that would really matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were interrogated by the one up there, the one -- the gentleman who is present here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you describe, perhaps. There are a lot of people on your left side.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a sick man who needs a good psychiatrist. It is a man with grey hair and glasses, and who is putting his -- who has his arm, his elbow on the desk, and his head is against his hand. That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Perhaps you can put precise on which bench or desk he is sitting, at which bench.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's sitting in the back row, in the back row. I don't know how else can I describe him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Just, Your Honour, for the record, Mr. Osmic identified a person who interrogated him on the 20th of April in Doljani, a person who is sitting on the back bench, and according to the description the witness has just given.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person you have identified now?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is Mladen Naletilic, called "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: When did you first hear his name?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name, I don't remember. But as for his nickname, he introduced himself to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Would you expand a little bit on that moment when Tuta introduced himself? If you remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as we were crossing that stadium, that football pitch, we were told that we were going to Tuta to be interrogated. We entered one by one, and Tuta was sitting inside and there was another young man there. I don't really know who it was, because I had never seen him before. It was dark and there was a candle burning. As far as I can remember, he offered us -- he offered me to sit down on a chair facing him, and this young man stood behind his back. And then Tuta introduced himself as a general, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did Tuta take any notes of the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really remember that he took any notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what about the other man who was present in that wooden room?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were only three of us: myself, Tuta and that young man, his bodyguard or whatever he was - I don't really know - so only the three of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did something special happen during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some bad things happened as far as I'm concerned. Nothing bad happened to them. They were fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... to you, I mean?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many bad things happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But perhaps you could recount what happened in that wooden room to you. What kind of bad things?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really like talking about some things, about details. But I'll mention one thing. It was cold, and there was a furnace -- a wood stove in a corner, and it was red hot because they were really feeding fuel wood into it. And at some point, that man of his pulled me by the hair and tried to put my face against the stove. And as I realised that I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. stood nothing to lose any more, I made a desperate effort, pulled myself back and pushed that man away from me, because he had brought my face so close to that stove, a centimetre perhaps or two, not more than that. And during this scuffle, the candle fell off the table and it became completely dark. So it ended well, as far as I'm concerned, because they threw me out -- they threw me out amongst other combatants, who then proceeded to beat me. I think this is enough about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was Tuta present at the moment when his bodyguard was mistreating you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd say that he was a good teacher, that is, the commander who gave them orders to do that. He did not stop him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the fish pond area?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about two or three hours. Not long.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see Tuta after the 20th of April?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were transferred to Heliodrom in Mostar --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: That's enough for a while. We'll return to this matter later on. So after two or three hours of detention in that area, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken in the direction of Ljubuski. That is, we did not know where they were taking us, but we eventually fetched up in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see any prisoners in Ljubuski who were detained there by the time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did. There were people crowded in small rooms. They couldn't even sit down. Most of them stood all the time, on their feet around the clock. And they put us in a separate cell, kind of a special treatment of theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see any other persons you were familiar before in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw those men from Sovici, that is, some of them. I saw them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you remember any names?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember those men well, because a day or two later, we could see one another, that is, all the prisoners, and there were about a hundred.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Right. Did you take -- did they take you outside to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went to work facing Serb lines, wherever. We were at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know who was in charge of Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How long did they keep you in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Ljubuski, we spent about two and-a-half months.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, we were promised we would be exchanged, but it was a trick. It was not true. We were taken to Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you just tell us, just in brief, about the conditions of life in Heliodrom for the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the accommodation, it was better than in Ljubuski. But in Ljubuski -- in Ljubuski, prisoners were left alone. And in contrast, in Mostar, it was a disaster.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you explain what do you mean by "disaster"?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first, we were forced to go to work. And whenever we would come out, you didn't know if you would return as an invalid or whether you would be brought back on a stretcher, or would you be buried somewhere, someplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you remember any of the places where the prisoners were taken to perform forced labour?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the prisoners, all prisoners were taken to forced labour; that is, nobody volunteered. And those places were from the airport, Hum, Stotka, Santic Street, Bulevar, Bijelo Polje, Dreznice, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see any military units deployed in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite a lot of soldiers passed through Heliodrom, but I don't remember particular units. Only on one occasion, I noticed during an action of the B and H army in the area of Hum and Stotka, some soldiers were killed on both sides, and we prisoners had to do our job. We had to retrieve the bodies. And then I noticed the Croatian army, who were called the Gromovi, "Thunders".

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you remember when -- the date that action took place?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not precisely. Whether it was July, I cannot tell you with precision, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Just some minutes ago, you told the Chamber that there was an occasion when you saw Tuta again. Could you recount that situation.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was at the time when one of the commanders of the B and H army called Jusuf Prazina, nicknamed, Juka, had some problems with the army. And when he joined the HVO in one of the units, one of Tuta's units, and then Tuta came to the Heliodrom to look for the prisoners from the -- from Stolac, Capljina, and wondered whether -- and asked whether some of the soldiers would like to join his unit. And it was then that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see him with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him personally. By some mistake, he entered our premises, which were located on the first floor. And the people from Stolac were on the floor above us. So I was in the corridor then, and I saw him, and I saw the people accompanying him because he never liked to walk alone. He must have felt afraid of being alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were you beaten in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was concerned, I, myself, was not beaten at Heliodrom, although I saw what happened to other people. Because on one occasion, they took out eight or nine people - I can't remember the exact number - and they were differently built, and they looked different, like we, here, in the courtroom. And when they returned, some were brought, some were dragged back, and some hobbled back. We could not recognise who was who, although we knew each other quite well. All over the bodies of these persons, there was no white flesh left. It was all black, the whole body was black.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were you kept in with other people from Sovici together?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were together, people from Sovici, from Prozor, and some people from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you remember if there was anything particular about prisoners from Sovici, Prozor, I mean prisoners from your cell?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we -- they were not different from other people. But only when someone had to be beaten up really well, then the people from Sovici and Prozor were their favourites.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were you taken to the confrontation line as well?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards all the dangerous lines in Mostar and the human shields, well, I was involved in both. And on one occasion, I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you give more details on the occasion you were wounded? When you were wounded, yes. When did it happen, in which place?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened on the 24th of September, 1993, in the area around the Bulevar. An action was taking place. I don't know where it all started from, on what side it started. We had certain duties to perform: to move the lines, to take out the dead and buried, to bring bags so that the HVO soldiers could capture territory with our assistance. And whilst we were transferring those bags with some vehicle, and on the way I was wounded. As there is always a silver lining in every cloud, at the time all the Muslims were thrown out of the hospitals. And when I say "every cloud has a silver lining," I mean on that particular day, at that particular hour, someone had forced them to return, to have these people returned to hospital, and that is how I came to be in hospital as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: When were you released from hospital?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was released in December when the exchange took place. As far as I can remember, it was on December 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: All right. And now I would like to return to the beginning of your testimony. Yesterday, you said that while talking about Sovici, you -- just to quote your words, "We defended again the people in the -- Croats and the foreign army that came there to attack the village." I would like you to explain, whom did you mean by "foreign army"?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was referring to those people who were not from that particular place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you mean -- I would like you to explain that particular place. Do you mean Sovici, or Jablanica, or something else? What do you mean, from a different place? Normally we say about foreigners -- you know in which sense?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know what a foreigner is. As regards the area of Sovici and Doljani, there was a regular army there, the army of -- the B and H army was there and the HVO army, and guards were organised around the village, not one from the others, to do something allegedly -- how can I say that? Preparations were under way to defend the area against the Serb enemy. And when a larger number of soldiers from the army came from the area of some other places, the beginning of an attack was actually being announced, because during the whole time people from Sovici would communicate amongst themselves and some noted the presence of an exterior army, as it were, which they felt was not necessary. I will not go into greater lengths on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. And again yesterday, just in the beginning of your testimony, you claimed that it was Tuta's unit that participated in the attack on Sovici. How did you learn it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was concerned, personally, I learned about that when I was arrested, because Tuta himself had told me that some of his best soldiers had been killed, though I personally feel that no Croatian soldier had been killed in Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. My examination-in-chief is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Osmic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: How are you today?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Al humdi'Allah," I'm well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Osmic, you have given three statements to various agencies or people concerning the events that you testified about today and yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the organisation, I don't really know how many there were. But whenever I was invited to say something on the subject, I always responded, because I believe it to be my duty, the duty of every man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall giving a statement in Mostar on the 19th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only remember the more important things that relate to the war. But I don't remember all those dates. But I was in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you remember a gentleman by the name of Ahmet Karic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall giving the statement in May 1995 or not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my statement in Mostar, yes, I did make that statement. But when it happened, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You were truthful in the statement you gave in Mostar, were you not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as truth is concerned, I'm a person who never lies, even when he's telling a joke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in 1995, the events which occurred in Mostar and Sovici in 1993 were much clearer in your mind than they are, say, today?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards more important events, my memory serves me well -- very well, whether it was in 1995. Or if I live another 50 years, I think I will recall all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you also gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in October of 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall a gentleman who interviewed you by the name of Romeo Ventura?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I vaguely remember the name. Romeo, Karic, and the gentleman there, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So you do recall making that statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I would ask you. Where do you recall you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my statements, I made them in Mostar, in Sarajevo, in Jablanica when I was going out. But there were people who collected information in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You also gave a statement in November of 2000, and the prosecutor Mr. Poriouvaev was present. Do you recall that statement?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just a moment ago, sir, when you greeted me, did you speak in Arabic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards my greetings to you, I addressed you in Bosnian. When you asked me how I was, I said "Al humdi'Allah," which is an expression I use frequently. And it is difficult to shred off habits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Have you had any contact with the Mujahedins?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war, I tried to refresh my religious knowledge, and I did have some contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And could you please tell me and tell this Trial Chamber when the first contact was and the location of that contact, please.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about in 1997 in Maglaj, a village by the name of Bocina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That village is located in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It is near Maglaj in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that contact?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a form of an abbreviated medresa, a religious teaching, because I was interested in that. I went there, I visited those people, and stayed some time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Something is wrong with the witness's microphone. We cannot hear him.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second time I stayed about four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Is the microphone working now for the witness? Can you test.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Witness will say something.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want me to say?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, it's working.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May the usher please put the ELMO down for me. Thank you. Thank somebody for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So the second occasion, you stayed four months with the Mujahedins. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can you please tell me how long you stayed on the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 45 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can you please, for my knowledge and the Trial Chamber, who are the Mujahedins?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, let me correct you. They are not Mujahedins. They are called Mujahedins. Well, they are people, just common people, with some religious knowledge, applying that knowledge. They are peaceful people. I think that is enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Are they also known as "holy warriors"?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. Depends on who calls them what.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But you were there for approximately six months on two occasions, and you are telling me that you do not know whether these Mujahedins are holy warriors or not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who is a holy warrior and who isn't. How can I know that? All I'm saying is they are just rank and file people, ordinary people, peaceful people who are not harming anyone, minding their own business, living, working, respecting one another, respecting commitments undertaken and agreements, who do not attack anyone, do not disparage anyone. And the kind of image you have of those people, I have no knowledge of that. Perhaps it wouldn't be bad for you if you met those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Perhaps. Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not armed. It was a village where religious education was organised, a Medresa. It was a religious school, and no weapons are taken to school. You should know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor is standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've got an objection. It seems to me that just for more than ten minutes they are talking here about things -- matters not relevant to the time frame of the indictment and to the events in the indictment, I mean that stretch in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I share the view expressed by the Prosecutor. I just wonder where you are going to lead us. Is that relevant to the actual facts of the indictment or to the incidents we discussed particularly today?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm finished, Your Honour, with that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I would just ask this witness:

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: During 1992 and 1993, in the war in the former Yugoslavia, were you aware that there were Mujahedins in the Bosnia-Herzegovina area?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know that. In late '95 is when I learned about those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on April 15th of 1993, you testified that you left your village to go to Sovici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And at that time, you were a member of the AbiH army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we were, in a way, so to speak, separated from the proper forces of the BH army and we could only maintain communication with the village of Sovici and Jablanica. But I was a member, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can you tell me and this Trial Chamber who ordered you to go to Sovici on April 15, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the order, nobody ordered us to do that. To begin with, we went to see what was going on there, because the shelling of Jablanica had started on the 15th of April and it is in the immediate vicinity, so that we wanted to know what would happen to us next if Jablanica and those other places fell into the hands of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could you please tell me how many kilometres it would have been from your home to Sovici?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, I'd tell you, but there are some other reasons for which I'd rather refrain from talking about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I'm just asking you how many kilometres from your village to Sovici, if you know.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you insist, then let me tell you precisely what the village is called, if you're all that interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Please, tell me the name of your village.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I'd like to cut this -- I deny you that pleasure because of some other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May we go into private session, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session. But I don't think the witness has understood clearly what your question is. Can you make it more clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please. We are in the open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: How many people set out with you on that day?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four. I was the fifth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you were armed, each and every one of you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, each one of us had some weapon; not much, but -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And each of you were in uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And your purpose to go to Sovici was to fight; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the reasons, a while ago you seemed to have a very poor memory, sir. First, to go and see what was going on there. That was the first reason. And, secondly, if need be, then to fight too, naturally, if we were to preserve -- to save ourselves and those people around us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you pass through Jablanica on your way to Sovici that day?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you meet any other soldiers from the AbiH army that day?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how shall I put it? It's a mountainous area. Not much traffic there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, I understand that, but did you meet any other soldiers that day?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not meet anyone that day, except when we arrived in Sovici and saw those troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Once you arrived in Sovici, you just indicated that you then observed troops. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And these troops were of the AbiH army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber the number of AbiH army troops that you observed that day in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as regards the number, in that area, there were perhaps about a hundred soldiers or so. Because a battalion -- it was 120, 130 soldiers because a battalion had just been formed. That is how many soldiers there were in the area of Sovici/Doljani. But I couldn't see all of them because people had been assigned to guard duty around the village, which means that I saw only some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Some of the people you couldn't see -- some of the soldiers you could not see that day because those soldiers were up in the mountains. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some guards up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see that it is 3.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Salko, I believe before we took the break, you had indicated that there was a battalion of the AbiH army consisting of approximately 120 or 130 soldiers in Sovici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, distinguished gentlemen, yes, sir, it was a rather small battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And will you please tell me and this Trial Chamber, of this 120 to 130 soldiers, how many of those were Croats?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were no Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could I have the usher put Exhibit P6.2 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Salko, do you recognise the village in that photograph? And for the record, that's P6.2.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could we have P6.3 then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Salko, for the record, you are now looking at Exhibit P6.3, and that's a photograph of the village of Sovici. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never seen this village from this particular angle to be quite sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave in 1995, and I believe in your testimony on direct examination, you indicated that there was an area called "Borovnik". Are you familiar with the area Borovnik, sir?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know -- I'd know it if I went to the village, then I'd know where the hill is. But like this, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Would you agree that Borovnik is a location on the hills surrounding Sovici?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I -- as far as I remember, it's a hill, Borovnik, even though I'm not all that familiar with those places, because it is, after all, another area. But Borovnik is where the Croat front lines were, towards Blidinje. I think it was the highest hill around Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And on that hill, the highest hill around Sovici, the AbiH army had troops, did they not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm repeating so as not to confuse all those hills. If I asked you now about some places -- I mean, I'm not really sure what they are called. It's only as far as I can remember, but that's not really reliable. I think that the HVO was on that particular hill, because if that is the hill which is closer to Blidinje, then it is. And if it is a hill that was closer to Prozor, then it was the BH army. That is all that I can tell you about this, because there were very many of those hills, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And are you familiar with an area around Sovici called Pasja Stijena?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes, yes. I do know it, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please explain to the Trial Chamber what exactly that consists of, since you know it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess it got its name because the boulders are quite big, although the first time -- when was that? Oh, yes, the 17th of April, that was the first time that I climbed that hill, and what I saw that day, that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That hill overlooks Sovici, does it not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, the name of that boulder is not only one boulder, it's quite long. Several -- no, perhaps a kilometre. Yes, you can see Sovici, but perhaps part of it but not the whole village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Salko, the Trial Chamber is unfamiliar with the geography of Sovici, so I would like to familiarise them with the geography. You understand?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I am not all that familiar with the Sovici geography either. I just told you, for the first time -- I climbed that mountain for the first time in my life then, and there are those boulders and hills with other names, so that I am really not able to tell you anything more about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm not curious about the names; that's not important. But is it a fair statement that Sovici is a village that is encircled by mountains?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll agree to that. I'm sorry to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know that this is Mr. Poriouvaev's witness, but there's a broader point to be made here, I'm afraid. Your Honour, there's no question that there were armed Muslims in the area of Sovici on this day, that some of them even shot back. That's not an issue in the case, it's not disputed, it is not a defence to any of the issues charged. The charges concerning Sovici are not unlawful attack. There's nothing to which these issues relate, it's not relevant, it's not a defence. And unfortunately, at the rate we're going, we're not going to get the witnesses finished this week, we're going to send witnesses home, and we're going on about issues which are non-issues, in fact, to the case. We admit Sovici is a small village surrounded by mountains, there were armed Muslims in the area, and there was some resistance in the area on the 17th and 18th of April, 1993. None of those facts are in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then I would also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, Mr. Meek, did you hear the objections from the Prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I didn't hear an objection, I heard a speech. But, Your Honour, if they also would stipulate that on that date, the 15th/16th day of April, 1994, that the entire village of Sovici was surrounded by armed Muslims, AbiH army, that's fine, I'll go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think we've already spent so much time on those circumstantial issues. I think the cross-examination should be more concentrated on the factual issues which are relevant in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So the Prosecutor does not stipulate to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not to that characterisation, no. I offered the facts that I offered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Salko, after you were captured, you have testified that you were taken to a small shack; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes, it is correct, it was a shack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And to make it clear, you never saw any fish pond there, did you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see it, that's true. But those others who were with me, the eight of them, naturally we talked on our way to Ljubuski, and that is how I learnt that there was also a fish pond there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And, Salko, you have made, and we have already established you have made, three separate statements either to the OTP or to the officials in Mostar. And would you agree with me that in none of those statements did you ever mention that my client, Mr. Naletilic, addressed you as "General Tuta"?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, and I said it in every one of my statements. Now, if somebody failed to take it down, that's another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in each one of those statements, you read those statements and you signed those statements as being complete and truthful and correct, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, is it important whether he introduced himself as a general or as a captain? He was there, and these are minor things, trivial things. But, yes, I did read these things and I signed it. I did not see anything that I did not like in those statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, to me it's important that the very first time you make this statement is in open court and never before in eight years. I'll go on. Salko, the other thing that you've indicated in your testimony today, that there was a gentleman with Mr. Naletilic in this shack that night, and you now claim today that this man tried to put your face against a hot stove. Did you make that allegation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And my question to you is: Why was that never told to any investigator in the three previous statements that you gave?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, what I have said now I have said in all three statements. Of course I mentioned only one thing that happened in that shack, one of the more terrible things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Salko, if I'm correct, on the 24th day of September, 1993, you were wounded in the area of the Bulevar in Mostar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on September 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And at the time that you were wounded, you were taking out bags Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. from an automobile; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I believe you testified on direct examination that you were -- while bringing bags from the vehicle, you were wounded. Did I misunderstand you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you didn't quite understand me. When we were transported together with those bags, I was wounded inside, in the vehicle itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. That clears that up. You were also then taken to a hospital in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You were treated for almost two months in that hospital in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Any other things about this -- strike that question. You testified that the Muslims had been forced from this hospital, but you don't know that personally; that's just something that you heard. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you are wrong. I saw that personally. When I came to the hospital, only one Muslim without one leg, a director or something, they left him there. I don't know why. I also saw how the Muslims were being taken out on stretchers with infusions, and I concluded that this actually happened before I was wounded, a day or so before I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You were immediately taken to the hospital and gained entry to the hospital, though, no problem?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, the day before or the two days before, I watched people being taken to the Heliodrom. They were left there in a corner somewhere with a drip, on stretchers. After the 24th of September, most probably someone issued a command that a certain number of persons should be taken back to hospital. When I came to hospital, I didn't see any Muslims in the hospital, apart from the person I mentioned with one leg. It was only later that they came, that they were coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Salko, I appreciate the answer. But my question was simply -- and I will state it again -- you were immediately taken to the hospital, and you gained entry with no problem, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that I've explained it to you quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Briefly, in Sovici, on the 15th day of April, 1993, did you observe the Croat flagged being burned?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: April 15th?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, the date that you were in Sovici, did you observe Croat flags being burned?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On April 15th, I was at home. On April 16th, I went to Sovici. And I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Were you in Sovici on the 16th of April when one Croat soldier was killed by a sniper and another Croat soldier had been wounded by a sniper?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where you get that information from. I cannot claim 100 percent. But in the conflict between the army and the HVO, I don't believe that any of the Croatian soldiers were killed. There were some stories told that some soldiers had come -- while they were cleaning the terrain, they came across some mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And I think I'm about finished. Salko, there were no Serbs within 50 kilometres of Sovici on April 15th, April 16th, or April 17th of 1993, were there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Salko, can you tell me, if you know, how many Croat civilians were in Sovici on the 16th day of April, 1993, when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many there were. The village was -- how should I say it? -- blocked. On the one side, there were the Croats, the Croatian army; and in the middle, there were the Muslims and the army. And so I couldn't go out and observe certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And I guess there's no cross-examination from the Defence counsel for Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right, Your Honour. The Defence of Vinko Martinovic, given the testimony of the witness, will not proceed to any cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Diarra has a question to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, you have spoken about your wound in a vehicle whilst transporting certain things and where you were fulfilling a mission. I would like to know how were you wounded, by what?

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was wounded from infantry weaponry. It must have been a special ammunition because it wounded -- some of my fingers were wounded, and the palm of my hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You spoke about confrontation between both sides on the front, and you said that you had been used for the purpose of retrieving bodies of the soldiers. You said that there were dead on both sides during the confrontation. But later on, when you listened to Tuta having said that he had lost many of his men, you said that you didn't believe him because, as far as you know, none of the Croatian soldiers had been killed. Was that because you were angry because it was said that both sides had casualties? So I would like to clear up the issue.

utterances.speaker: SALKO OSMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards Doljani and Sovici, this is quite a different story. I was speaking about events in Mostar, because I could not work as a prisoner in Sovici and Doljani because I was free then. All this happened in Mostar, the human shields, retrieving bodies, recovering the wounded. I said about the clashes in Sovici, when I was speaking about that, I was still free, so I wasn't called upon to recover the wounded and the killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much for helping us by giving the evidence. We wish you good luck. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So, Mr. Prosecutor, who will be your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness will be asking for again a pseudonym and for his facial image to be distorted, so we'll have to make the arrangements, if there's no objection or if the protections are granted, before we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there is no objections from the Defence side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we're getting the witness - excuse me, I apologise for my voice - we can tender to the Court -- the Court asked, in connection with a prior witness, that a statement be -- a copy of the statement be provided, and we prepared that. What has been done, Your Honours, is because the statement was much more extensive on other topics and other issues besides that which were put to the witness in her testimony, we've included those parts of the statement that related to the testimony that she gave. So I can provide those to your staff at this time. I guess the usher is not here at the moment, so those can be provided. With the Registry's assistance again, perhaps -- okay. I can provide to the Chamber and to counsel and others a proposed order of witnesses, taking us through the latter part of October. This will give you an idea of the witnesses we've called so far, which are also listed, and where we expect to go in the next few weeks, accounting for that we will not be in session of course next week, and then some of the other weeks will also be short weeks. So I hope that's of some assistance to you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you brief us on the relevance of the indictment to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, this witness will be testifying concerning, in particular, allegations concerning superior authority, paragraphs 14 and 17; count 1, paragraph 25, 27, 33 to 34; and I would say "topically," if I can, about the attack on Sovici, and forced labour and beatings. And as we stated during our Opening Statement, Your Honour, we would try, to the extent possible, to submit the case to the Chamber in units or chapters, if you will. And starting with the last witness, we have moved primarily into the area of Sovici and will present several witnesses dealing with the area of Sovici, although again, as we discussed during the Opening Statement, of course many of their stories start in Sovici but then they go to a number of other places. Many of them, for instance, wind up at the Heliodrom and on the confrontation line in Mostar as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, while we are waiting, I would like to put a question to my colleague with regard to a witness. And I suggest we go into a private session, because there has been some confusion and I would like to clear this up. It is only because of the name of one of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we into the private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper shown by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you are going to be shown now a piece of paper on which your name is written. You have been granted protections by the Chamber, including the protection that your real name will not be used in the record to protect your identity. Your face will also be protected. So what the usher is going to put in front of you now is a piece of paper that has your name on it, and you will be referred to, for purposes here, as "Witness W". But I want you just simply to say " "yes" or "no", is that your name? And don't use your name, because we are trying to protect your name. Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, I have a feeling that you're going to need to move in closer to the microphones, please. Witness W, I want to ask you, as we start, in terms of reference, should it come up for the purposes of examination before the Chamber, do you have any preference if you are addressed or referred to as a "Bosniak" or a "Muslim" or any other term?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I would like to be referred to as a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, directing your attention to the days before approximately the 17th of April, 1993, you were a member of the Territorial Defence around the area of Sovici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct to say that during the earlier days of the Territorial Defence, that it consisted of both Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the Territorial Defence, or TO, prior to mid-April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Before mid-April, the aim was to, along with the Croats, we keep guard -- how could I say it -- against some enemy. We didn't have very much information about the enemy. But at the moment, we gathered together and stood together, and we had one defence. And then we were all invited to come, and we were -- and we were given these invitations by someone called Kopilas, Stipo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, you referred to the enemy during that time period. Who, generally, or what group or military force are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: At that time, it was the case of the Serb attack against the B and H.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness W, can you assist the Chamber, please, if you know, approximately how many Bosniak families were living in Sovici, in the Sovici area, around mid-April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: There were between 150 and 200 families living in Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have any information that you can provide us, please, in terms of the number of Croat families that were living in the Sovici area around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, frankly, I'm not quite sure. But there were some, about -- between 50 and 70 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, who was the commander of the Bosniak component of the Territorial Defence, if there was one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before the 17th of April, 1993, did you have any idea of what would happen in those days following? Did you have some idea or any warning of what would happen in those next several days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, what happened on the morning of 17 April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: That morning, I had just woken up. I was drinking coffee with my wife when the shelling started. Then I jumped up with my wife. I took a

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness W, I'm going to pause you for a moment. When you refer to some of these places and other persons who may be close to you, it is probably better if you do not use their names as it may tend to lead to the identification of yourself as well. There may be some points, if necessary, we will go into private session. I think for now, you and your wife and your 50-day-old baby went to another house after the attack started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I heard you, but it didn't come through the translation, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: That day, from the morning until the evening, shelling around the village -- shelling of the village never stopped. And we could see shells falling around the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you able to tell from which direction the attack came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: One could see that, because the shells were passing by the house so that one could conclude that the shells were coming from Risovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were you able to observe that day any particular type of weapons that were used during the attack? And I'm primarily directing your attention now to heavy weapons. I'm not talking about infantry weapons, but if you know any type of heavy weapons that were used during the attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. I saw you were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, the witness just indicated that he believed shelling was coming from, and the transcript does not show what location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Scott could clear it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, did you say "Risovac"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that spelled R-i-s-o-v-a-c?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, were you able to observe any of the heavy weapons that were used during the attack that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Towards the end of the attack, a tank came down to so-called Obruc, and we could see it from the cellar of that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you involved in any way as a combatant that day? Did you at all lift a weapon? Were you engaged in the fighting that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I had an M-48 rifle, but I never left the cellar that day. Because I could not come out, as they were on both sides. So there was no way for me to come out of the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: From the extent that you can say so, based on your observations on that day, can you characterize for the Chamber the nature of any defence that the Bosniak side put up to the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: They were very -- there was very little resistance to this attack by people who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know whether at some time during the course of the day there was an order on the Bosniak side to surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: In late afternoon, around 5.00 or around that time, the commander came up, and we learned from him that we were to hand over our weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And approximately -- all right. And that was approximately around 5.00 or 1700 hours on the 17th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: That's right, yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you able to identify, from what you saw or in the events that happened immediately thereafter, what military unit or units were attacking or had attacked Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: That evening, after we had handed over our weapons, we went there, we turned -- we -- at the stream before the school, a vehicle was there awaiting us, and somebody was noting down the weapons that we were turning over. At Pole's house, we turned over the weapons that we had and the ammunition, and some were beaten a little and some were ill-treated a little. But that evening, they took us to the school and put us in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a moment, please. Just so the record is clear, when you said a moment ago -- I think you said -- it's not in the record, so I can't be exactly sure. But did you say the name of this person was "Stipo"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Stipe Pole is -- it was Stipe Pole's house next to the stream where we handed over the weapons. But then we passed by that house and went on to the school, where they detained us and guarded us that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we get to the Sovici school, let me go back to the question I put to you a moment ago. Did you become aware around this time the identity of the forces that had attacked Sovici that day and that you in fact were surrendering to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Not that evening. It was only in the morning, as they began to arrive. They introduced themselves, and it was then that we learned who had attacked Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what did you learn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: And one called "Robo", he introduced himself and told us that they were Tuta's troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you hear this Robo say anything more, make any other statements that identified these troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, he didn't talk much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sorry. We seem to have some problems with the French translation because the sound echoes in the earphones. It may be some mechanical problem. It's okay? Yes, it's okay. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, Witness. You started to give an answer, but let me just pose the question to you again. Did you hear this Robo say anything more or make any other statements that identified these troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, he didn't talk much at that time as we were gathering there and he was -- because he was bringing some people in and bringing back those who were trying to escape a little until everybody was gathered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And how would you describe this man named "Robo", if you can?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Rather short but overweight. That is, he was -- and somewhere he had found a green beret, I mean a cap, which he put on, and that is how one could recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness W, before we go to the Sovici school: When you left your house, when you were taken out of the house and you went to the school, did you go through parts of the village of Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, what was the condition of the houses in Sovici when you passed through the village at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: But I was passing by Croat houses all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, what was the condition of those houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, naturally like today. Nobody ever touched them, not a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. bullet nor anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you also have the occasion to pass by houses which you knew to be Bosniak, that is, where people of Bosniak ethnicity lived or resided?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Only the next day, when I went to the house I was born in, I saw that it had been hit by a shell, but not much. It hit the edge of the house and that was it. Not much damage was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, let me come at it this way: Did there come a time when you learned - and then we'll work backwards - that the houses of the village had been destroyed or burnt down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: But we learned that when we were in the camp at Ljubuski, that the houses had been set on fire and destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Had the houses been burned and destroyed as of the time that you were arrested and taken to the Sovici school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: The houses were not destroyed whilst we were in Sovici. Those houses were destroyed after we were taken to the camp in Ljubuski and women and children taken to Krcevine - that is what I stated before and will state now - and elderly and other men were kept in the school, and that is when those schools were burned and destroyed, razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber whether any members of your family were in a -- and again don't use any names, but any members of your family were in fact in a house at the time that it was set on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I learned that after I came out of the camp. I learned it from my wife. When they were putting fire to houses, her and the 50-day-old baby and her mother were in the house when they opened fire from the vicinity and set the house on fire with incendiary bullets. And my wife, her mother and the baby were in the house then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you were passing through Sovici on the late afternoon of the 17th of April, could you see the mosque in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you come to know later that the mosque had been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I learned it in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you remember, did anyone tell you when it had been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, not the date. All I learned was that it had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Apart from the date, can you assist us, please, do you know whether it was destroyed after the time that you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: It was destroyed while these old and invalid women and children were still there. That is when it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When was that in relation to the time that you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: A few days later, when we were driven off to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Will you tell the Chamber, please, to your knowledge, was the mosque in Sovici ever used for any military purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During these days around Sovici, did you ever know a man named Marko Rozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sure, we will redact it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was -- and not in relation to yourself, but generally speaking, who was Mr. Rozic in terms of did he hold any positions in that area around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: At that time, Marko Rozic was something like the Minister of Defence in the Sovici HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to ask the usher's assistance, please, if I can, to distribute Exhibit 56 to both the Chamber and counsel. This will have been in Binder Number 1; but again, simply to make things a bit smoother, I'll provide working copies at this time. If one of those could be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I believe we can use the ELMO, Witness W, because nothing, I don't think, on the ELMO or anything that you say about it would tend to identify you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can have some assistance, please, on the ELMO. I see Mr. Krsnik is on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We objected to this document during the depositions. We did that also in writing. We object to using this document in evidence because a witness who wanted to prove the authenticity of this document during the depositions said that he found it in a newspaper. And we filed our objection within the time -- within the necessary time limit. We objected to its being produced in evidence. That was in July, so we still object to the production of this document until there is a ruling on our motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott. Do you have anything to say about this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was offered before. It was shown to a witness. I'm showing it to this witness. I may show it to five more witnesses, until such time as the Chamber is satisfied that a foundation has been laid. I think this witness can assist us, if there is any valid objection to it, which we disagree with. But I think this witness can provide information about the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, the Prosecutor told us that this witness will provide more information about the authenticity of this document, so why not allow this witness to show us his knowledge about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence objected as soon as this document was shown to a witness who was to confirm the authenticity of the document. In our motion in writing, we lay the foundation for our objection. It is difficult to understand, Mr. President, that a document of this nature be carried by a daily and that then somebody claims that it is authentic. Of course, I will go by your decision. If you decide to admit this document, we shall write another motion, then, because we still can write down all our objections to various exhibits of the Prosecution, and we shall then mention this one once again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think now the question is not to admit this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. document into evidence or not, but just to call the witness to prove the authenticity of this document and for us to get more information about this document. So we'll use this document but not as evidence at this moment. Is that all right, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Mr. Scott, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness W, the first thing I would like you to do, please, if on the ELMO you can focus on that part of the first page of Exhibit P56, that is a photograph. If you can, can you identify that person to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: This is Marko Rozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is this the same man that you testified about a moment ago who you described as the HVO Minister of Defence in the Sovici area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
