utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. President, it may be that we should go to private session just for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness W, what happened after you arrived at the Sovici school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: When we got to the school, in front of the school the people that they were bringing in the school -- to the school, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, don't use their names. You can just say your brothers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I saw them being tied to a plum tree in the vicinity, but I didn't dare look, really. I just glimpsed. I saw, when they were hit, that they fell to the ground, and then I couldn't look any more. Then a little later, a few minutes later, I looked again, and then I saw that Roda [as interpreted] beat them. And when I looked again, the other two were standing next to him, and then I didn't look any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said just now, I think it came out in the transcript as "Roda". Did you see -- one of the men hitting your brothers, was he one of the men that you identified a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: You're referring to Marko Rozic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies. Was this the same person who you identified as "Robo"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, later when I looked, it wasn't Robo. Robo had gone. But the other two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Going back in the sequence of events, you told us that you looked up or looked out several times. In that sequence of events, did you ever see Robo as one of the persons who was beating your brothers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, it was -- Roba beat him the first time. And then when I looked the second time, Roba was no longer there. There was someone else beating them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe to the Chamber how it was that these men were being beaten? What was being done to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, first of all when I looked, I glimpsed, there were shovels -- they were hit by shovels and by guns, by the butts of the guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you spent one night at the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what happened the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, we spent the night there, and the next day we were questioned. And other people who remained there were brought. People who were hiding, they were brought in the evening. We were lined up in front of this school, and then we set out for Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we go on to Ljubuski, can you tell the Chamber, please, when was the last time during these events that you saw your wife and child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, before I set out on that day in the morning, about 10.00 a.m., I went to buy some breakfast, to have something to eat, and that was the last time I saw her until I returned from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you were held until the 1st of March, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you did not see your wife and child again until sometime after the 1st of March, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: On March 1st, 1994, in the evening, about 6.00, 7.00 p.m. when we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what happened to them after you last saw them? That is, back during the time when you were in Sovici and after you saw them, did you learn what happened to your family after you were put on the bus to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, we didn't know anything until one of the guards told us that they had been expelled in the direction of Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: From Makljen -- I don't know which one it was, but I know it was the first place in the direction of Bugojno from Makljen. I think it's Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Going back to being taken from the school, can you tell the Chamber, did you see anyone in front of the school whose identity you came to know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: In front of the school, there was Rogic, who sent us to the camp in Ljubuski. Cikota, so-called "Cikota", Tuta's commander, he wanted to show, with a sign of his hand, to let us go home. But Rogic at the moment said, "No, to the Ljubuski prison."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did anything happen as you were loaded on the bus? Were any of the prisoners mistreated at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Before we got into the bus in front of Stipe Pole's house, the bus stood there. And once we were going into the bus, climbing into the bus, Muharem Helbet was mistreated, and Lulic -- I don't know his name. He was under age, he was a minor. Roba actually stabbed Muharem with a knife in his leg. And when Dzemo was climbing in, he was also hit. And then Mustafa Kukic and Lulic came. And when he was brought into the bus, the doors of the bus were shut, and the bus left for Doljani and then subsequently to Risovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you know the name of the man who stabbed Helbet in the leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: It was Roba.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you able to identify -- let me back up. When you were put on the bus, were there HVO guards, soldiers, on the bus with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, there were four of them, including Roba.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you know what unit, what military unit these soldiers were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: They belonged to Tuta's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber how were you treated on the bus trip -- there may be various stages of that -- but as you were moving along on the bus, how were you treated by these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: How they treated us, well, they beat us. They made us sing songs, they did all sorts of things until the bus stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a minute. My apology. When you said they made you sing, what did they make you sing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Ustasha songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "Ustasha songs"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: The songs that were sung and which we sang were -- how can I explain -- exclusively songs for the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how did you feel about being forced to sing those songs? How did that impact you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: We had to sing because we didn't want to be beaten. It was under pressure that we had to sing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was anything said to you by any of the HVO soldiers about that? Do you recall anything in particular that was said to you while you were singing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: They kept saying, Stronger and stronger, stronger. And this is the word that they would use, Louder and louder. That's what they would be saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You started to say a moment ago, before I interrupted you - my apology - that the bus stopped, then, at one point. And can you tell us what happened when the bus stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: The bus stopped. We were driven out of the bus, and they were watching for no one to escape because it was already dark. They lined us up in two rows, and they were standing in front of us. Dzemo and -- and they took persons out of the line up, they were beaten. And while we were waiting there, Dzemo and Zijad were being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to that in a moment, if we have time. But before that, when the group of you were standing in the two rows, was anything done toward all of you as a group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: As a group -- well, actually it happened to Zijad and Dzemo, because he was in the HVO unit. They mistreated him there. They used sniper methods. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to stop in just one moment, Mr. President, if I can just clarify this one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were any weapons fired when you got off the bus at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, when they were lining us up, on the way out, one of them said, "Who dares run away will have to contend with gunfire," and he started shooting in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can probably stop there for the day, if that's agreeable to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll adjourn to 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
